messages.author: a27a46fa1c1d735a
messages.subject: Re: Showing off ggplot2
parts:
> I started using ggplot2 in school to make great graphics that were
> betterthan what my classmates were creating and I'm now using it in the
> "real-world". I want to talk about ggplot2 at our next R users group and
> was curious what you guys would recommend showing off. What do you think
> coolest ggplot2 functions and graphics are?

Start with a bare scatter plot and show them how to add shape and colour
aesthetics and faceting. Also you may get ideas from here:

http://learnr.wordpress.com/tag/ggplot2/

Finally, if you want to "show off" I would change the default theme and use
one without a background or grid lines, it makes the plots look nicer and
cleaner. But this is just my opinion of course :-)

messages.author: 8ffd6137fd43c6df
messages.subject: Re: Showing off ggplot2
parts:
I like Baptiste's advice, and suggest adding a side-by-side comparison of the ggplot and base code (if you think it's appropriate for the audience).  From my perspective, it's not that ggplot can do things base graphics can't.  It's that it can generate a publication quality graph in 10 lines of code that requires base graphics at least 60.  Even more if you're faceting with a common x & y scale, and want to suppress the redundant axes in between the panels (eg, Baptiste's slide 14).

And as others have said before, the easier a graph is to produce & later modify coherently, the more thoroughly you can explore and describe the space.  I think thi s is important even if the graphs are seen by only your research team.
